content: Singapore's digital economy reached 18.6% of GDP in 2024, up from 14.9% in 2019. More than two-thirds of digital growth comes from non-ICT sectors including Finance, Wholesale Trade, and Manufacturing, showing that digital transformation is an economy-wide phenomenon.

Singapore's tech workforce grew from 208,300 in 2023 to 214,000 in 2024. Roles in AI/Data and Cybersecurity are among the fastest growing segments. Median monthly wage for resident tech workers is S$7,950, significantly above the national median of S$4,860.

14.5% of Singapore SMEs adopted AI in 2024, up from 4.2% in 2023 — a 3.5x increase in one year. More than two-thirds of AI-adopting firms plan to prioritise workforce training and upskilling in the next 1-2 years.

Singapore's National AI Strategy 2.0 aims to triple the local AI practitioner pool to 15,000 by 2026. IMDA is introducing AI fluency programmes for the tech workforce, including training software engineers to become full-stack developers capable of orchestrating AI agent systems.

Over 4,000 cybersecurity roles remain unfilled in Singapore as of late 2025, with 400-800 new job vacancies posted monthly. The cybersecurity workforce has grown from 4,000 in 2016 to 12,000 in 2022, but demand continues to outpace supply.

Ministry of Manpower placed four cybersecurity roles on Singapore's 2026 Shortage Occupation List (SOL), creating local-first hiring pressure. In-demand roles include forensic analysts, penetration testers, cyber engineers, and security architects.

64% of cybersecurity professionals in Singapore report experiencing burnout, citing the unrelenting pace and complexity of cyber threats. 53% plan to leave their current roles within the next year, exacerbating the talent shortage.
Cybersecurity engineers in Singapore now earn a median monthly salary of S$8,000, placing them in the Top 20 highest-paying professions on par with risk managers and legal counsel.
source: MOM 2024 Occupational Wages via Centre for Cybersecurity

content: Emerging hybrid Cyber-AI roles are growing rapidly in Singapore including AI Security Specialists, Security Data Analysts, and Automation/Detection Engineers. Over 80% of large Singapore enterprises have adopted cloud solutions, driving demand for cloud security skills.
source: ITEL 2026 Cybersecurity and AI Hiring Trends

content: AI and tech-specific skills dominate Singapore job postings in 2025-2026. Demand is rising for Python, SQL, cloud technologies, and AI/ML skills while traditional web development skills are becoming less prominent.

Professionals with expertise in AI/ML, cybersecurity, and cloud technologies can expect salary premiums of 15-25% across industries in Singapore. Specialised roles in AI engineering, cybersecurity, and green energy command salary jumps of 8-12%, well above the national average of 4%.
Singapore's wage forecast for 2026 is 4.0-4.3% average increase across all sectors. Healthcare leads with ~6%, followed by IT/AI at 4-6%, Banking/Finance at 3-5%, and Manufacturing at ~4%.
CSA launched the OT Cybersecurity Masterplan 2024 and OTCEP Forum to strengthen cyber defence for critical industrial systems including energy, water, and transportation infrastructure in Singapore.

SANS Institute and GIAC will deliver four fully AI-focused cybersecurity certifications by end of 2026, covering offensive AI, red team automation, model integrity, and AI-driven operations — reflecting the convergence of AI and cybersecurity skills.

Finance & Insurance remains Singapore's largest digital economy contributor with a median monthly salary of S$8,950. The sector is investing heavily in AI for risk management, fraud detection, and algorithmic trading.
95% of Singapore SMEs are now onboard with digitalisation, accelerating demand for cloud, cybersecurity, and data analytics services across all industries.

Production LLM deployment has created demand for new skills in Singapore: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), vector databases, prompt engineering, LLM evaluation, and guardrails implementation. ML engineers who can build reliable LLM-powered applications are commanding top-tier compensation.

Southeast Asia's digital banking sector continues rapid growth with Singapore as the regional hub. Digital banks and payment platforms are hiring engineers with experience in high-availability systems, regulatory compliance (MAS guidelines), and real-time payment processing.
